request.spec:
Show on each person their settled-total (the due of their SETTLED claims that count, at
their frozen figures, corrections included) and their open-total (the due of their OPEN and
PENDING claims that count: a held, deferred or retired-and-excluded claim is left out as it is
from the due-total). Show the sheet's settled-total and open-total too, each simply everyone's
figure added up (not trimmed). The two must add up to the person's untrimmed due-total before the
cap.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Show on each person their settled-total (the due of their SETTLED claims that count, at
their frozen figures, corrections included) and their open-total (the due of their OPEN and
PENDING claims that count: a held, deferred or retired-and-excluded claim is left out as it is
from the due-total). Show the sheet's settled-total and open-total too, each simply everyone's
figure added up (not trimmed). The two must add up to the person's untrimmed due-total before the
cap.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Each person row now shows a settled-total and an open-total, and the sheet shows both totals too. All 4 acceptance tests pass under `bin/e2e`.

**How it's worked out:**
- **Person settled-total:** adds up the due on each SETTLED claim at its frozen figure. Corrections are included.
- **Person open-total:** adds up the due on each OPEN and PENDING claim. Held, deferred and retired-and-excluded claims are left out, the same way the due-total leaves them out.
- **Sheet totals:** every person's figure added up, with no trimming.

Both totals use the same list of counted claims and the same per-claim due as the due-total. So for each person they always add up to the due-total before the cap.

When a claim has no due (n/a), it is skipped, so a person whose due-total shows n/a gets 0.00 for both — which is what the test expects.

The change is front end only. The figures are worked out in the browser, as the due-total already was, and the test expects no new audit records, so nothing changed in the server, stored data or audit file.

**What changed:**
- `src/main/frontend/features/rates/rates.ts`: two new functions, `personStatusSum` (one person's total) and `sheetStatusSum` (the sheet's total).
- `src/main/frontend/features/rates/rates.slot.tsx`: two new components, `PersonStatusTotals` on each person row and `StatusTotals` on the sheet, placed just after the due-total.
